defect.kind: product (live-proven S25+, this hour — nine card approvals, nine deadlocks)
defect.summary: The owner's card-typed secret was a SUBSTRING of the page URL (http://127.0.0.1:8099/login.html — e.g. "login"), and every post-approval state build threw 'app-authored section (URL) would carry a credential-secret value'. Structural insight: the builder only knows SANCTIONED (card-typed) secrets, so the app-authored throw could only ever fire on sanctioned values — i.e. it could only deadlock the run on collisions (URL/goal/title substrings) and never catch a genuine leak (an unsanctioned secret is by construction unknown to the builder). The throw was dead weight that kills; masking is the lawful response everywhere.
